facts.fact_text: On 6 May 2012 a public demonstration entitled the 'March of Millions' was held in central Moscow.
The march on 6 May 2012 was peaceful and held without any disruptions.
According to the applicant, on 6 May 2012 he arrived at Kaluzhskaya Square to take part in the 'March of Millions' march.
According to the applicant, on 6 May 2012 he walked down Yakimanka Street to Bolotnaya Square.
According to the applicant, on 6 May 2012 he passed the metal detectors at Bolotnaya Square and joined other protestors in front of the stage, where a rock group was performing.
According to the applicant, at around 7.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 groups of police officers started pushing into the crowd, forcing it apart by using their truncheons.
When the marchers arrived at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, it became apparent that barriers installed by the police had narrowed the entrance to the meeting venue.
The barriers installed by the police at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 allegedly restricted the space allocated for the meeting.
To control the crowd at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, the police cordon forced the protestors to remain within the barriers.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police ordered the meeting at Bolotnaya Square to finish early.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police began to disperse the participants of the meeting at Bolotnaya Square.
According to the applicant, at around 7.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 groups of police officers started pushing into the crowd, forcing it apart by using their truncheons.
According to the applicant, protestors at Bolotnaya Square were surrounded and squeezed together by police officers.
According to the applicant, at some point he realised that he was facing the police line and that the police were using excessive force to arrest protestors.
According to the applicant, he was both angered and scared by the actions of the police and actively resisted.
The applicant was eventually seized by four police officers and escorted to a police car, which took him to a police station.

On 6 May 2012 the Moscow city department of the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation opened criminal proceedings to investigate suspected violence against the police under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
On 28 May 2012 a criminal investigation was launched into the offence of organising acts of mass disorder under Article 212 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.
On 28 May 2012 the two criminal cases (concerning mass disorder and organising mass disorder) were joined into a single case.
On 5 June 2012 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (use of violence against a public official).
The applicant was accused of active resistance to police officers on 6 May 2012.

The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its order of 30 May 2012, referred to the gravity of the charges against the applicant.

The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its order of 30 May 2012, stated that if the applicant was at liberty he could co-ordinate his position with accomplices whose identities were still being established by the investigation.

The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its order of 30 May 2012, pointed out that the applicant had forcefully resisted the police officers during his arrest, which had led to them using force and handcuffs against him.

The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its order of 30 May 2012, relied on information obtained from undercover sources that the applicant had connections with football fans and groups of anarchists.

The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its order of 30 May 2012, concluded that there were sufficient reasons to believe that the applicant was likely to abscond, continue his criminal activity, threaten witnesses, destroy evidence or otherwise obstruct the course of the criminal proceedings.
The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its order of 30 May 2012, dismissed a request from the applicant for an alternative preventive measure.

The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow, in its extension order of 4 July 2012, relied on the gravity of the charges and information on the applicant's character, which gave it sufficient grounds to presume that he might reoffend, threaten witnesses and other participants of the criminal proceedings, destroy evidence or otherwise obstruct the proper administration of justice.

On 31 October 2012 the Basmannyy District Court of Moscow extended the applicant's pre-trial detention until 6 March 2013, referring to the gravity of the charges and the complexity of the criminal investigation.

The Moscow City Court, in its extension order of 23 April 2013, reiterated the grounds given in the previous extension orders and stated that the circumstances justifying the detention order had not changed.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow, in its extension order of 6 June 2013, based its decision on the gravity of the charges, the finding that 'the reasons which initially warranted the detention have not changed', and that 'no other measures of restraint would secure the aims and goals of the judicial proceedings'.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow, in its extension order of 19 November 2013, based its decision on the gravity of the charges and the nature of the offences imputable to the defendants.
